title: The Hound of the Baskervilles (Oxford Bookworms 4)
creator: Arthur Conan Doyle, graded retelling
why: A short, plotty mystery in 1,400 headwords: pure speed practice.

title: A graded tech biography (Steve Jobs or Bill Gates)
creator: Penguin or Macmillan Readers, upper levels
why: Tech founders in simple English; check the catalogue for the title.

title: Oxford Bookworms Factfiles (science and tech)
creator: Oxford University Press
why: Short non-fiction on science topics, easy enough to read fast.

title: Cambridge Discovery Readers (Upper Intermediate)
creator: Cambridge University Press
why: Graded non-fiction with many topics; good for a calm reading habit.

title: The Giver
creator: Lois Lowry
why: A short dystopia with short sentences: real fiction that still reads fast.

title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
creator: J. K. Rowling
why: Huge learner community and an audiobook; NGSL covers about 93% of it.

title: Holes
creator: Louis Sachar
why: Plain, funny and plotty: a great book to build a reading streak.

title: Flowers for Algernon
creator: Daniel Keyes
why: Sci-fi about the brain, and the narrator's English gets better as you read.

title: Ender's Game
creator: Orson Scott Card
why: Strategy games, a genius kid and space: reads like a long game session.

title: Who Moved My Cheese?
creator: Spencer Johnson
why: A tiny workplace story about change; you can finish it in a few days.

title: Ready Player One
creator: Ernest Cline
why: Online worlds and gamer culture; the 80s references are the hard part, not the words.

title: The Martian
creator: Andy Weir
why: An engineer solving one problem at a time, with a programmer's humour.

title: Project Hail Mary
creator: Andy Weir
why: Same easy voice as The Martian, with more science and a great friendship.

title: The Phoenix Project
creator: Gene Kim, Kevin Behr, George Spafford
why: A DevOps novel full of the words of your meetings: outage, deploy, stakeholders, escalate.

title: The Goal
creator: Eliyahu M. Goldratt
why: A factory novel about bottlenecks; the style is old but the ideas are useful at work.

title: Atomic Habits
creator: James Clear
why: Short chapters and a clear structure, and the ideas help with ADHD routines.

title: Deep Work
creator: Cal Newport
why: About attention and focus at work: useful words for talking about how you work.

title: The Pragmatic Programmer
creator: Andrew Hunt, David Thomas
why: Words you half-know from code, now in full sentences you can reuse in reviews.

title: The Lean Startup
creator: Eric Ries
why: Startup words you hear in product meetings: pivot, runway, iterate, validate.

title: Zero to One
creator: Peter Thiel, Blake Masters
why: Short and opinionated: good for practising how to agree and disagree.

title: Educated
creator: Tara Westover
why: A powerful memoir with rich everyday words, not technical ones.

title: Surely You're Joking, Mr. Feynman!
creator: Richard P. Feynman
why: Funny science stories told the way people speak: great for natural phrases.

title: Shoe Dog
creator: Phil Knight
why: A founder's memoir with business words in a friendly, conversational voice.

title: Steve Jobs
creator: Walter Isaacson
why: Long, so read it in chunks; the story of Apple in clear journalist English.

title: Hackers & Painters (Paul Graham essays)
creator: Paul Graham
why: Essays you can read one at a time online: perfect for 15-minute sessions.

title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
creator: Daniel Kahneman
why: Dense, but words like bias and heuristic come up in every discussion.

title: Why We Sleep
creator: Matthew Walker
why: Popular brain science, and sleep matters for memory and for learning words.

title: Driven to Distraction
creator: Edward M. Hallowell, John J. Ratey
why: About ADHD, written to be encouraging: personal and motivating.

title: The Innovators
creator: Walter Isaacson
why: The history of computers and the internet, told through the people who built them.

title: Life 3.0
creator: Max Tegmark
why: The big questions about AI, with words you can use in AI meetings.

title: The Hard Thing About Hard Things
creator: Ben Horowitz
why: Frank management language: how leaders really talk when things go wrong.

title: Sapiens
creator: Yuval Noah Harari
why: Big ideas in abstract English: great practice for C1 reading and linking ideas.

title: Gödel, Escher, Bach
creator: Douglas Hofstadter
why: A goal book about minds and machines; not a first C1 book.

title: Range
creator: David Epstein
why: Why generalists do well at work; good ideas for career talks.

title: The Idea Factory
creator: Jon Gertner
why: The story of Bell Labs, where the transistor and much of modern tech began.

title: Co-Intelligence
creator: Ethan Mollick
why: Recent and practical: how to work with AI, the topic of many of your meetings.

title: The Alignment Problem
creator: Brian Christian
why: A deep look at how AI learns values; dense, so keep it for later.

title: Superforecasting
creator: Philip E. Tetlock, Dan Gardner
why: How good predictions are made; useful words for planning and estimates.

title: BBC 6 Minute English
creator: BBC Learning English
why: Six minutes, a word list and a transcript: the easiest daily listening habit.

title: English at Work
creator: BBC Learning English
why: A short office drama that teaches meeting and email phrases.

title: All Ears English
creator: Lindsay McMahon, Michelle Kaplan
why: American English for work and social life, including meeting expressions.

title: Better @ English
creator: Lucy and Ken
why: Natural conversations with transcripts and vocabulary notes.

title: Plain English
creator: Jeff Brown
why: Current news read a little slower than normal: real topics, easier speed.

title: Syntax
creator: Wes Bos, Scott Tolinski
why: Two web developers talking fast and informal: the register of tech teams.

title: JS Party
creator: Changelog Media
why: A panel of developers: good practice for following several speakers.

title: The Changelog
creator: Changelog Media
why: Interviews about open source and software careers.

title: The Daily
creator: The New York Times
why: Clear studio speech about one news story a day.

title: Short Wave
creator: NPR
why: Short science stories with clear voices; one episode fits a coffee break.

title: Planet Money
creator: NPR
why: Economics told as stories: business words in a fun way.

title: Software Engineering Daily
creator: Software Engineering Daily
why: Interviews with real technical depth, like a long architecture meeting.

title: Hanselminutes
creator: Scott Hanselman
why: Friendly tech interviews with a calm host; good for interview-style English.

title: Lex Fridman Podcast
creator: Lex Fridman
why: Long talks about AI and science; very hard, so try 15 minutes at a time.

title: Huberman Lab
creator: Andrew Huberman
why: Neuroscience for daily life; dense and long, but on your favourite topic.

title: Acquired
creator: Ben Gilbert, David Rosenthal
why: Deep stories of great tech companies; start with a company you love.

title: Rachel's English
creator: Rachel Smith
why: American pronunciation, step by step: helps people understand you in calls.

title: English with Lucy
creator: Lucy Earl
why: Clear lessons on phrases and common mistakes.

title: Speak English with Vanessa
creator: Vanessa
why: Everyday and business phrases with slow, clear speech.

title: Fireship
creator: Jeff Delaney
why: Fast, funny 100-second tech videos: hard speed, words you already know.

title: Veritasium
creator: Derek Muller
why: Science with great visuals and human-edited captions.

title: Kurzgesagt – In a Nutshell
creator: Kurzgesagt
why: Beautiful animations make dense science easy to follow.

title: CGP Grey
creator: CGP Grey
why: Fast but very clear explanations of how systems work.

title: Computerphile
creator: University of Nottingham
why: Computer scientists explaining ideas on paper, the way you explain at work.

title: Lex Clips
creator: Lex Fridman
why: Short parts of long AI talks: real speech in small pieces.

title: Y Combinator talks
creator: Y Combinator
why: Founders and partners speaking: the register of pitches and product reviews.

title: WWDC and Google I/O developer talks
creator: Apple, Google
why: Engineers presenting work with slides, just like a team demo.
